The complete guide to IMS

A clear, step-by-step reference to everything the Studio Lotus IT Inventory Management System does — with real screenshots of the live system, covering every module and every role.

📖 Read start-to-finish or jump around 🖼️ Real screenshots of the live system 👥 Role-by-role 🖨️ Print / save as PDF anytime
How to read this guide. Coloured boxes mean: 💡 Tip a shortcut, ⚠️ Careful something to double-check, ℹ️ Good to know background. Each module also shows a “Who can do this” line so you always know if it’s for you. Click any screenshot to enlarge it.

The big picture

What is IMS, in one breath?

IMS is Studio Lotus’ single home for every piece of IT kit the studio owns — laptops, monitors, servers, printers, software licences, cables and paper — plus who has it, what it cost, when its warranty ends, and what it needs next.

🏷️

Every item, one tag

Each device gets an automatic tag like SL-LAP-2026-0001 and a QR sticker. Scan it to find anything in seconds.

🤝

Who has what

Hand a laptop to a colleague (“check out”), take it back (“check in”). Every handover is logged forever.

🛡️

Nothing slips

Warranties expiring, licences renewing, stock running low, repairs overdue — IMS warns you before it hurts.

💰

Money in view

Book value, yearly spend, budget vs actual and a 5-year hardware/software forecast — all calculated for you.

🔧

Full life story

Purchase → in use → repair → retirement. Each asset carries its own history and invoices.

📊

Answers, not spreadsheets

Dashboards and reports replace the old “which sheet was that in?” hunt.

You don’t need to be “technical.” IMS was built to be obvious. Pick a module from the left, follow the numbered steps, done. This guide never assumes you’ve seen it before.

Orientation

The 5-minute tour

You reach IMS in your browser, sign in with your Studio Lotus Google account, and land on a screen that always looks the same. Learn these three areas once and every page makes sense.

Step 1 · Sign in

Only studiolotus.in accounts work. A personal Gmail will be turned away. If you’re signed into several Google accounts, pick the work one.

Step 2 · Learn the screen

①

Left sidebar

Your list of modules — Dashboard, Assets, Allotments and so on. What you see here depends on your role. An Admin group appears only for managers and admins.

②

Top bar

The Scan tag / serial box (type or scan a code and hit Enter to jump straight to that item) and, on the right, your name and role with a Sign-out button.

③

Main area

The working area. Lists have a search bar and filters; forms have friendly labels; most actions are one orange button away.

The scan box is everywhere. A cheap USB barcode scanner “types” the code for you and presses Enter — IMS opens that exact asset. No scanner? Just type the tag or serial and press Enter.

Permissions

Who can do what

IMS gives each person exactly the buttons they need — no more. Your role (shown next to your name, top-right) decides what you can see and change. Here are the six roles, from most to least powerful.

Super Admin

Runs the whole platform

Studio Lotus platform owners

  • Everything below, across all Studio Lotus apps
  • Manage people & access levels
  • The only role that sees User management
IMS Admin

Owns IMS end-to-end

Head of IT

  • All inventory actions + delete assets
  • Set budgets and financial settings
  • Manage master data (categories, vendors…)
IMS Manager

Day-to-day owner

IT lead / office manager

  • Everything an Operator can do
  • Edit master data & see Finance / Reports
  • Can’t delete assets or manage platform users
IMS Operator

Hands-on the kit

IT support staff

  • Add & edit assets, print labels
  • Check out / in, transfers, repairs
  • Record purchases, licence seats, stock
IMS Viewer

Look, don’t touch

Finance/ops who need visibility

  • Browse assets, dashboard & alerts
  • Export lists to CSV
  • Cannot change anything
Employee

Just “My Assets”

Everyone at the studio

  • See the kit issued to you
  • Acknowledge a handover
  • Nothing else in IMS
Roles stack. Each role can do everything the one below it can, plus a little more: Employee → Viewer → Operator → Manager → Admin → Super Admin.

The basics behind everything

Asset tags & the life of an asset

Two ideas power the whole system: every asset gets a smart tag, and every asset moves through a simple set of statuses. Understand these and nothing else will surprise you.

Anatomy of an asset tag

You never type a tag. IMS builds the next one automatically the moment you pick a category. It can’t clash and you can’t fat-finger it. Each category has its own code — LAP laptop, MON monitor, SRV server, and so on.

The life of an asset (its “status”)

A brand-new device starts In stock. Give it to someone → Assigned. Take it back → In stock. Something breaks → In repair → back to stock (or its owner). When it’s written off → Retired or Lost. IMS moves the status for you as you use each module.

The modules, one by one

Every screen, explained

Below is every module in the sidebar. Each has a real screenshot, a “who can do this” line, and numbered steps. Sections are collapsible — click a heading to open or close it.

1

Dashboard

the morning glance▸

Your home page. One look tells you how healthy the estate is: how many assets, what they’re worth, how many are out with people, what’s in repair, this year’s spend, and anything that needs attention.

Who can do this: Viewer and everyone above. Read-only for all.
Read it left-to-right, top-to-bottom. Numbers first, then the bars show the shape of your estate, then the amber/red list tells you what to act on today. Hit Refresh for the latest.
2

Assets — the live register

find anything▸

The master list of every device. Search, filter, scan, export, and open any item to see its full story.

View: Viewer+  ·  Add / edit: Operator+  ·  Delete: Admin+
  1. Search

    Type a tag, serial, model or a person’s name in the search box — the list filters instantly.

  2. Filter

    Narrow by category (Laptop, Monitor…) or status (In stock, Assigned, In repair…) with the two dropdowns.

  3. Scan to jump

    Point a scanner at a QR/barcode (or type the code) in the top Scan box and press Enter — IMS opens that exact asset.

  4. Open an item

    Click any row to see its full detail page.

  5. Export

    Click CSV to download exactly what’s on screen (filters included) for Excel or Finance.

The green/red pills in Warranty mean In warranty or Expired — worked out automatically from the purchase date.
3

Add an asset

the guided wizard▸

Register a new device in under a minute. The form is split into three friendly parts and fills in as much as it can for you.

Who can do this: Operator and above.
  1. Pick the category

    Choose e.g. Laptop. The Auto asset tag appears at once — you can’t mistype it.

  2. Pick the model (optional)

    If the model is in the catalogue, choose it and the maker, specs and warranty length auto-fill. Not there? Type the model name.

  3. Scan / type the serial

    Scan the device’s barcode into the Serial number box, or type it.

  4. Condition & location

    Set condition (New, Good…) and where it lives.

  5. Purchase details

    Vendor, cost and purchase date. From the date, IMS auto-calculates warranty end and depreciation.

  6. Save

    Hit Save asset. You land on its detail page with a ready-to-print QR label.

Fill in cost + date. They power warranty alerts, book value and the finance charts. An asset with them missing shows up as a “data gap” alert.
4

Asset detail & QR label

one item, full story▸

Everything about a single asset on one page: overview, financials & warranty, and a scannable label.

View: Viewer+  ·  Edit: Operator+  ·  Delete: Admin+
  1. Read the two cards

    Left = what it is and who has it. Right = money and warranty, including days left.

  2. Edit

    Operator+ — click Edit to fix any field (status, condition, location, cost…).

  3. Print the label

    Click Print label for a sticker with the tag, serial and QR — ready for a label printer or A4 sheet.

  4. Delete

    Admin only — the red bin removes an asset (it’s hidden, not truly erased, so history is safe).

Deleting is rare. A device that’s dead or sold should usually be Retired (via Edit ▸ status), not deleted — that keeps it in the records and the money history intact.
5

Allotments — issue & return

who has what▸

Hand kit to people and take it back, with a permanent handover trail. “Check out” = give; “Check in” = return.

Who can do this: Operator+  ·  View history: Viewer+
  1. Check out

    Pick an available asset, search the staff directory for the person, optionally set a location and note, then Check out. The asset flips to Assigned.

  2. Check in

    In Currently held, click Check in next to the returned item. It goes back to In stock.

  3. Transfer

    Moving kit between people or sites is logged too — from an asset you can re-assign without a full return.

  4. Trace it

    The Handover history shows every check-out/in with who, when, and whether the person acknowledged.

Only “In stock” items can be checked out. If a laptop is already Assigned or In repair, check it in / return it first.
6

Repairs

send out, bring back▸

Track anything that goes out for service: the fault, the vendor, expected return, and the final cost when it’s back.

Who can do this: Operator+  ·  View: Viewer+
  1. Send it out

    Pick the asset, describe the fault, choose the service vendor, set an expected return date and (if known) an estimate. Save — the asset becomes In repair.

  2. Watch the queue

    Open repairs sit at the top. Anything past its expected date gets an Overdue flag (and an alert).

  3. Mark returned

    When it’s back, click Mark returned, choose the outcome (Repaired, Replaced, Beyond repair…), enter the final cost and new condition. The asset returns to stock or its owner.

Final cost feeds Finance. Repair costs show up in the cost ledger and this year’s spend automatically.
7

Purchases

bills & invoices▸

Record what you bought and file the invoice straight to the shared Google Drive — no more lost PDFs.

Who can do this: Operator+  ·  View: Viewer+
  1. Record the bill

    Fill in vendor, invoice number, date and total. Optionally link it to the asset it paid for. Save.

  2. Attach the invoice

    Click Attach on the row and pick the PDF/photo. IMS uploads it to Google Drive and links it — click View on Drive anytime.

Link the bill to its asset. That stamps the cost and date onto the asset so its book value and warranty stay correct.
8

Licenses

software & seats▸

Track software subscriptions, when they renew, and which colleague holds each seat.

Who can do this: Operator+ (add & assign seats)  ·  View: Viewer+
  1. Add a licence

    Name it (e.g. Adobe Creative Cloud), set vendor, billing cycle, number of seats, cost and renewal date.

  2. Assign seats

    Click Seats, search a colleague and Assign. The used/total bar updates. It won’t let you over-allocate.

  3. Release a seat

    When someone leaves or no longer needs it, Release frees the seat for reuse.

A renewal within ~45–90 days turns amber and raises a renewal alert so you’re never surprised by an auto-charge.
9

Consumables

bulk stock▸

Things you count rather than tag — paper, toner, cables, spare mice. Track how much is on hand and get warned before you run out.

Who can do this: Operator+  ·  View: Viewer+
  1. Add an item

    Name it, set the unit (pcs, ream…), starting quantity and a minimum level (the point below which it’s “low”).

  2. Receive or issue

    Click Receive / issue and choose IN (stock arrived), OUT (handed out) or Adjust (stock-take), with a quantity.

  3. Watch the flag

    Drop to or below the minimum and it turns LOW and raises a low-stock alert.

10

Finance

the money view▸

This year’s spend, budget vs actual, a full cost ledger, and a five-year hardware-vs-software forecast.

Who can do this: Manager+  ·  Set budgets: Admin+
  1. Read the four tiles

    FY spend, budget, variance (green = under budget) and next-year forecast.

  2. See where money goes

    Spend by type splits purchases, licence renewals and repairs. The 5-year projection predicts refresh & renewal costs (orange = hardware, blue = software).

  3. Export

    Export CSV hands the whole cost ledger to Finance.

You don’t enter these numbers — IMS calculates them from your assets, purchases, licences and repairs. Keep those tidy and Finance is always right.
11

Reports

deeper cuts▸

Ready-made breakdowns: warranty health, spend by category, allotment activity, and licence/stock summaries.

Who can do this: Manager+
Use Reports for the “how are we doing overall?” questions; use Assets + CSV when you need the row-by-row detail.
12

Alerts

before it bites▸

Your to-do list, generated automatically. Four kinds: warranty expiring, licence renewing, stock low, repair overdue — plus “data gaps” where an asset is missing key info.

Who can do this: Viewer+
Work the red list first. High-priority means money or downtime is at stake soon — a renewal about to auto-charge, a repair past due, stock at zero.
13

My Assets

for every employee▸

The one page every colleague can use — a simple list of the kit currently issued to you.

Who can do this: Every employee (and everyone above).
Something wrong? If a device you have isn’t listed (or one you returned still shows), tell IT — they’ll correct the handover in Allotments.
14

Admin · User management

people & access▸

Where the platform owner sees who can get in and at what level. Shared across all Studio Lotus apps, not just IMS.

Who can do this: Super Admin only.
Need more access? This is the page a Super Admin uses to grant it. Everyone else should just ask them.
15

Admin · IMS settings (master data)

the autofill engine▸

The lists that make the rest of IMS smart: categories, manufacturers, vendors, locations and the product catalogue. Set these up well and adding assets becomes almost automatic.

Who can do this: Manager+
  • Categories — each has a tag code (LAP, MON…), default warranty months and useful life used for tags, warranty & depreciation.
  • Manufacturers & Vendors — the makers and the shops you buy/service through.
  • Locations — offices, floors, rooms and stores.
  • Products — the catalogue of specific models. Add a model once and every future asset of it auto-fills.
Best-practice. Add a product to the catalogue the first time you buy a model. From then on, adding those assets is: pick category → pick model → scan serial → save.

Terms & definitions

Glossary

TermWhat it means
AssetAny single tracked device — a laptop, monitor, server, printer, UPS, etc.
Asset tagThe auto-generated ID like SL-LAP-2026-0001 printed on the label. Never changes.
StatusIN STOCK on the shelf · ASSIGNED someone has it · IN REPAIR out for service · RETIRED/LOST end of life.
ConditionPhysical state: New, Good, Fair, Poor, Damaged.
Check out / inGiving an asset to a person (out) and taking it back (in). Both are logged.
Book valueWhat the asset is “worth” today after depreciation — cost minus wear over its useful life.
Warranty statusIn warranty or Expired, worked out from purchase date + the category’s warranty months.
Seat (licence)One person’s slot on a software subscription. 25 seats = up to 25 people.
ConsumableBulk stock counted by quantity (paper, toner, cables), not individually tagged.
Data gapAn alert that an asset is missing key info (serial, cost or date) — fill it in to clear it.
Financial year (FY)Runs April→March. FY 2026 = Apr 2026 to Mar 2027. Used in tags and finance.
Master dataThe background lists (categories, vendors, products…) that make autofill work.

When something’s odd

FAQ & quick fixes

“It won’t let me sign in”

Use your @studiolotus.in Google account, not a personal one. Signed into several? Pick the work account on the Google screen.

“I can’t see Finance / an Admin menu”

That’s your role. Finance & Reports need Manager; User management is Super Admin. Ask IT to adjust your access.

“The button I need is greyed out or missing”

Same reason — role. Hand the task to someone with the right level, or request an upgrade.

“I can’t check out a laptop”

It’s probably already Assigned or In repair. Only In stock items can be checked out — return it first.

“My Assets shows the wrong kit”

Handover records are off. Ask IT to check it in / out correctly in Allotments.

“The finance numbers look wrong”

They’re calculated from assets, purchases & repairs. A missing cost/date is usually the cause — look for data-gap alerts and fill them in.

“I got a warranty / renewal alert”

That’s IMS doing its job — act before the date. Renew the licence, or plan the replacement.

“Do I have to type the tag?”

Never. Tags are generated automatically; you only ever scan or click them.

Remember

  • Sign in with your @studiolotus.in Google account.
  • Your role (top-right) decides what you can do.
  • Tags are automatic — never typed.
  • Only In-stock items can be checked out.
  • Retire, don’t delete, dead assets.
  • Fill in cost & date so money & warranty stay right.
  • Work the red alerts first.
  • Stuck? It’s usually your access level — ask IT.
